entries.name: TU-134A-3
entries.variant: Tupolev Tu-134 with D-30 engines (first D-30 series, 72 passengers, maximum takeoff weight 44,000 kg), as described in the USSR Ministry of Civil Aviation's 1967 Provisional Instructions for Operational Flight and Piloting; NOT the later Tu-134A-3 (47,000 kg, D-30 Series III)

sources.title: The Tu-134 Aircraft with D-30 Engines, Provisional Instructions for Operational Flight and Piloting, Book 1, 2nd edition (English-language version), revised and supplemented by USSR Ministry of Civil Aviation Order No. 625 of 19 Sept 1967; CIA Reading Room document CIA-RDP78-03066R000400020001-4
sources.publisher: USSR Ministry of Civil Aviation (original); translation declassified and released by the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (government publication)
sources.page: Section 1, Ch. 1 Flight Restrictions: 3. Altitude Restrictions, Table 3 (printed p. 38); 5. Aircraft Weight Limitations; 6. Power-plant Limitations; 7. Various Restrictions item 2 (crosswind) and item 5 (cabin pressure differential). Section 2, Ch. 2: 6. Level Flight (p. 244); 11. The Descent (pp. 256-257). Introduction (p. 16-17, pressurized fuselage)

pressurised.note: Section 1, Ch. 1, 7. Various Restrictions: 'Operational cabin-pressure differential: 0.57 atm'; introduction refers to 'the pressurized section of the fuselage'.

cruise_kts.calculation: Section 2, Ch. 2, 6. Level Flight (p. 244): 'The cruising speed of the aircraft is 780-870 kilometers per hour'; ranges are quoted for cruising speeds of 850 and 770 km/h. 850 km/h / 1.852 = 458.96 -> 459 kt (km/h to knots only).
cruise_kts.note: Published as a range 780-870 km/h (421-470 kt) with no stated Mach number or TAS/IAS; the same passage quotes range for cruising speeds of 850 and 770 km/h. 850 km/h is taken as the typical (faster) planning speed, not the midpoint of the range (midpoint 825 km/h = 445 kt); 850 km/h at 11,000 m is about M0.80, in line with the manual's descent Mach 0.80-0.82, so it reads as TAS. Variant is the 44 t Tu-134 with D-30, not the A-3 (rule 5 fallback).

ceiling_ft.calculation: Section 1, Ch. 1, 3. Altitude Restrictions, Table 3: allowance-limit altitude 11,000 m at 42 t flying weight, 11,500 m at 39 t, 12,000 m at 36 t and less. Maximum 12,000 m / 0.3048 = 39,370 ft.
ceiling_ft.note: Table 3 gives the 'allowance-limit altitude' by flying weight: 11,000 m at 42 t, 11,500 m at 39 t, 12,000 m at 36 t and less (no row for the 44 t maximum). It is the manual's maximum permitted flight altitude, weight-limited, not a certified single figure; the type's highest permitted altitude (12,000 m) is used as the maximum operating altitude, reachable only at 36 t or less. Reference sites (not accepted) give 12,100 m for the Tu-134A.

max_xwind_kts.calculation: Section 1, Ch. 1, 7. Various Restrictions item 2: 'Maximum allowance for crosswind during takeoff and landing is 14 m/sec.' 14 m/s x 1.94384 = 27.2 -> 27 kt (m/s to knots only).
max_xwind_kts.note: Manual limit, not a demonstrated value: 'Maximum allowance for crosswind during takeoff and landing is 14 m/sec' (Section 1 Ch. 1 item 7); Section 2 repeats 14 m/s on a concrete runway for takeoff (6 m/s ice-covered) and 14 m/s lateral component for landing. Dry-runway value used. Variant is the 44 t Tu-134 with D-30.

cruise_alt_ft.calculation: Section 2, Ch. 2, 6. Level Flight (p. 244): 'the cruising altitude of the TU-134 with D-30 engines in level flight is 11,000 meters'. 11,000 m / 0.3048 = 36,089 ft -> 36,000 ft (nearest 500).

climb_fpm.note: Airliner class preset; the climb graphs (Section 3, Figs 3.19-3.26) are not in the translated book.

climb_kts.note: Airliner preset fraction 0.9 x cruise 459 kt = 413.1 -> 415 kt (nearest 5).

descent_fpm.calculation: Section 2, Ch. 2, 11. The Descent (pp. 256-257): vertical speed 10-14 m/s down to 5,000 m, 12-16 m/s below 5,000 m. Using mid-values 12 and 14 m/s from the cruising altitude of 11,000 m: 6,000 m / 12 = 500 s; 5,000 m / 14 = 357 s; total 857 s; 11,000 m / 857 s = 12.83 m/s x 196.85 = 2,526 fpm -> 2,500 fpm.
descent_fpm.note: The manual states these as the vertical speeds of the normal descent procedure (idle/81-83% mode); mid-values of its ranges are averaged. Cruise 11,000 m is the manual's own cruising altitude.

entries.name: TU-154B2
entries.variant: Tupolev Tu-154B-2 (three-engine medium-haul airliner; empty weight 50,700 kg, maximum takeoff weight 98,000 kg per the Russian Ministry of Defence)

sources.page: Технические характеристики: 'Масса, кг: пустого самолета / максимальная взлетная 50 700 / 98 000'; 'Крейсерская скорость, км/ч 950'; 'Практическая дальность, км 3500'

cruise_kts.note: Headline cruise speed; the page names neither a Mach number nor an altitude or power setting. Other sources found (reference sites and encyclopedias, not accepted) give 850-950 km/h, so the figure may be a maximum-cruise figure.

cruise_alt_ft.note: Airliner class preset 35,000 ft would apply to a pressurised jet, but no accepted source states that the Tu-154B-2 is pressurised, so the table's rule for an unpressurised or unknown type lowers it to 12,000 ft. The Tu-154 is in fact a pressurised jet that cruises near 9,000-11,000 m; the lead should see check_notes.

climb_fpm.note: Airliner class preset; no published time to climb.

climb_kts.note: Airliner preset fraction 0.9 x cruise 513 kt = 461.7 -> 460 kt (nearest 5).

descent_fpm.note: Airliner class preset; no published descent rate.
